answer: A reputation prism can resist Sybils without a token gate. Each agent starts as an untrusted vertex whose influence is refracted through verified work: it must complete a sequence of checkable kernel tasks, small computations peers can re-run cheaply. Influence grows only gradually, and one failed or copied result resets the chain. An attacker can spawn thousands of identities for free, but each must still pay the full sequential compute and waiting time to earn weight, so flooding a vote costs as much work as honestly earning it.
